“It was after the end of the First Age that the great power and wealth of Moria began, for it was enriched by many folk and much lore and craft, when the ancient cities of Nogrod and Belegost were ruined in the change of the western world and the breaking of Morgoth.” — HoME XII, The Peoples of Middle-earth [C]
in Ered Luin and not in Beleriand: ruined in the upheaval rather than drowned with the land, its folk removing to Khazad-dum after the First Age ended

timeline.cite: App B, the Tale of Years, Second Age, 'c. 40' [C] — 'Many Dwarves leaving their old cities in Ered Luin go to Moria and swell its numbers'. THE ARCHIVE'S OWN LABEL S.A. c.40 IS THAT ANNAL'S YEAR VERBATIM, and it was cited to App A III, which carries NO YEAR: its whole dating is 'After the end of the First Age'. The tenth instance of that substitution after 426, 433, 434 and 437–439. THE OTHER CLAUSE HAS A DIFFERENT SOURCE AGAIN: 'Ered Luin broken … tumults' is Silm 24 — 'In the Great Battle and the tumults of the fall of Thangorodrim … the walls of Ered Luin were broken' — and NO ANNAL DATES THE RUIN OF THE TWO CITIES: App B names Nogrod and Belegost 0 times in 44,662 characters and never mentions the War of Wrath. [I-M] on the identification: the annal says 'their old cities in Ered Luin' and does not name them; App A III names them, undated
timeline.what: Ered Luin broken in the War of Wrath's tumults; many remove to Khazad-dûm
